clue.text: Stand out, being, so to speak, extra large

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the clothing-size letters are to be pronounced rather than written

parts.note: XL is the clothing-size label for extra large

explanation.surface: Someone big who is conspicuous in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Say XL out loud and it gives the five-letter verb; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine above others is to be outstanding, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Kit and Sally accompanying me into hospital department

indicators.note: into places the joke and me inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
a sally is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Kit and Sally, two people, coming with me into a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit and Sally read like names; Kit is the definition and Sally a quip. 'accompanying' just joins QUIP and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is gear, the tools and apparatus needed for a task.

clue.text: Dismiss bank official

definitions.meaning: to discharge someone from service, especially the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to expel from service; the noun is a teller handling a bank's money.

clue.text: This is applied to speed in major road with lights around

indicators.note: around says the lighting word goes round the road letter

parts.note: lit means having lights on
the M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: A speed restriction on a big lit road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. The major road is the M1, Britain's first motorway, with its figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed cap is the maximum allowed, applied to how fast drivers go.

clue.text: Gaelic leader has to fall back into his native tongue — it's incomprehensible

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word Gaelic

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the language word

parts.note: the Gael's own tongue here is Irish

indicators.note: back says the word for fall is read from right to left

parts.note: to ebb is to fall, as a tide does

explanation.surface: A Gaelic speaker lapses into his own language and nobody follows him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for fall before 'into' puts it inside the language; 'has to' is a link, and the definition includes 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless babble is a thing no one can understand, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Stuff contained in bulging hamper

indicators.note: contained in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Things packed in an overfull picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff here means fabric; gingham is a checked cotton cloth.

clue.text: Sort of attire bishop's got on top?

definitions.text: Sort of attire bishop's got on top?

indicators.note: got on top puts the bishop letter at the head of the down entry

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: Sort of suggests the letters are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: Wondering what kind of hat a bishop wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges ATTIRE into IRETTA, below B; the whole clue also defines the clerical cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn on the head by Catholic clergy, so headgear a prelate might wear.

clue.text: Spinning wheels used before in another site

indicators.note: Spinning suggests the letters are whirled around into a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Wheels that once turned are now used somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' turns WHEELS into ELSEWH; 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere different, at another place.

clue.text: I am going to river shortly for dip

parts.note: I'm is a contraction of I am

indicators.note: shortly says the river's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the Mersey is the river at Liverpool

explanation.surface: Someone heading to the river for a quick swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip something is to plunge it briefly into liquid.

clue.text: It's difficult having nothing in stock

indicators.note: in puts the zero inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: It is hard when your stock is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile, a store kept in reserve.

clue.text: Stars represented in our arms

indicators.note: represented hints the letters are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A coat of arms bearing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges IN OUR ARMS into the constellation's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Bear is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Dance music composed by a doctor in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the doctor piece inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A tune written for dancing by a South African physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed by' is just linking padding here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian rhythm used for ballroom dancing and its accompanying tunes.

clue.text: Produce monochrome urban picture, and celebrate

definitions.meaning: literally, colour a whole city scene one shade, scarlet
go out and have a riotous night of fun

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out partying wildly; read literally it means colouring a city scene entirely crimson.

clue.text: Turned silent about a bishop's mistake

indicators.note: Turned says the whole assembled piece is read from right to left
about puts the following pieces inside the word for silent

parts.note: mute means silent
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop's blunder that left someone speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A RR in MUTE to give MUTARRE, and 'Turned' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: An error, especially one listed as a correction in a printed book.

clue.text: At sea, catch line of a particular craft

indicators.note: At sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fisherman's catch line for a certain kind of boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat; it means a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical describes what belongs to a specialist skill or trade.

clue.text: Times carrying article from abroad that's never stale?

indicators.note: carrying says the word for times holds the article within it

parts.note: ages are long times
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper running a foreign piece that never goes out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition; 'Times' is not the newspaper but AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never grows old or tired, so it cannot go stale.

clue.text: Principal part of stockade, to wit, fencing

indicators.note: Principal part of points to the leading letter of the word

parts.note: wit is clever play on words

explanation.surface: Most of a stockade is fencing, that is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'fencing' looks like the stockade's palings but is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing is the sport of fighting with blades, i.e. blade combat.

clue.text: Explorer sent back to take care of Virginia, say

indicators.note: sent back says the explorer's name is read from right to left

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian-born explorer who sailed for England
c/o, care of, is the address abbreviation

explanation.surface: An explorer returns to look after the American colony of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns CABOT into TOBAC. Virginia is a type of the leaf, not the US state, though the surface wants the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a variety of the smoking leaf, so it is an example.

clue.text: Proudly stand up for City, nonetheless last in table

indicators.note: read as none-less, it says the zero-shaped letter is dropped from the city

parts.note: Bristol is a city in south-west England

indicators.note: last in picks out the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A fan proudly rising for their city team though it is bottom of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' reads as O-less: O (nothing) leaves BRISTOL, giving BRISTL.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to stiffen up, as hair does, or to draw oneself up indignantly.

clue.text: Source of music on a vehicle I entered

indicators.note: entered says the vehicle and I go inside the words on a

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Music coming from a car someone got into.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR I goes into ON A after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument, which produces tunes.

clue.text: Artist's link with merchant of Venice

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant and traveller

explanation.surface: A painter connected with Shakespeare's play about a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Shakespeare's Shylock, but the merchant is Marco Polo.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: A bird or two

parts.note: a tit is one small bird
a lark is a second, songbird

explanation.surface: Spotting one bird, or maybe a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or two' says the answer is two birds joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A titlark is a pipit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Well-rounded character, but terribly moronic

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone well-rounded but awfully stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a Greek letter, not a person; the round O is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is written as a circle, so a rounded letter.

clue.text: Risk overstepping the mark and being taken aback

definitions.meaning: behave close to the limits of what is acceptable
in sailing, a ship is taken aback when the wind catches its sails from the front, a hazard when steering too close to it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to court danger or impropriety; literally it is steering a vessel so close to the breeze it risks stalling.

clue.text: Splashes water on clothes issued to sailors

definitions.meaning: old naval term for ready-made clothing and bedding supplied to seamen

explanation.definitionFit: The verb is to spill liquid about; the noun is naval issue clothing.

clue.text: Crew audibly scoffed

indicators.note: audibly says a word for scoffed is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A team of rowers loudly mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mocked but means ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat's team of oarsmen numbers eight, so the crew takes the number.

clue.text: Choose one constant measuring device

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, a constant

explanation.surface: Picking a single unchanging instrument for measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is the British pub device fixed to an upside-down spirits bottle that dispenses an exact measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar gadget gauges a fixed tot of spirits, so it is a dispenser that measures.

clue.text: Involved with launch in Russian river after a month

indicators.note: after places the river behind the month

parts.note: Aug is short for August
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: Taking part in a ship's launch on a Russian river a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaugural means relating to an opening or first beginning, such as a launch.

clue.text: Woman will provide support for old sailor

parts.note: she'll is a contraction of she will
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A woman promises to back an elderly seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'LL loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellback is slang for a veteran seaman, especially one who has crossed the equator.

clue.text: Fish in barrel taken to US city

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A fish packed in a cask shipped to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunny is an older name for the tuna, a large sea fish.
